title: From questions to clean events
subtitle: An Amplitude workshop for digital analytics practitioners
technical_level: Practitioners who can design a schema and configure a browser SDK without writing application code
outcomes: Move from a funnel drop-off to evidence about what users did next
Design event names, event properties, and user properties for a small product
Connect a browser app to a new Amplitude project and inspect live events
materials: A laptop with a current browser
An Amplitude account that can create a project
Permission to use the workshop app and open Amplitude in another tab

run_of_show.title: Reset and open the workshop hub
Station 1: Choose events
run_of_show.done_when: Every chosen action has one event name and one question it will answer.

run_of_show.title: Station 2: Add properties
run_of_show.done_when: Each event carries the context its question needs, and the user properties describe the person rather than the latest action.

run_of_show.title: Station 3: Connect Amplitude
run_of_show.done_when: The app shows Connected and the Activity panel records an Identify call.

run_of_show.title: Station 4: Generate and verify events
run_of_show.done_when: At least three event types appear in Amplitude with the event and property names you planned.

run_of_show.title: Station 5: Ask one question
run_of_show.done_when: A chart answers one question from your plan and its limitation is written down.

actions.question: How often do people add work, and from which entry point?
Which tasks get completed, and how long does completion take?
How often do people reverse a completion?
How much correction happens after task creation?
Do people remove active work or clean up completed work?
Which view helps people manage their list?
What state are lists in when people share them?
Do shared links bring another person into the product?

slides.title: From questions to clean events
slides.subtitle: A two-hour Amplitude workshop for digital analytics practitioners
slides.notes: Welcome the room. The first hour follows one analysis from a funnel into qualitative evidence, paths, activation, and an experiment. The second hour starts with a finished app. Attendees make the measurement decisions and then watch their events arrive in Amplitude.

slides.title: Two hours, two modes

points.title: Follow the evidence
points.body: Funnel → replay → journeys → cohort → guide experiment

points.title: Build the data
points.body: Plan a schema, connect the app, and inspect live events

slides.notes: Set expectations. The tour moves quickly and uses a prepared project. Questions that need a longer product detour go into the break or closing minutes.

slides.title: Funnel Analysis
points: Build the critical path with a clear conversion window
Break down the largest drop by a useful property
Open the dropped-off users in Microscope
slides.notes: LIVE DEMO. Start from the prepared activation funnel. State the decision the chart supports before changing controls. Show the largest drop, add one breakdown, then open Microscope on the drop-off. Keep the chart measured as Conversion so replay is available. CUT: skip the breakdown and go straight from the drop to Microscope.

slides.title: Session Replay
points: Watch a session from the funnel drop-off
Jump to the moment of friction
Check whether the behavior suggests a testable explanation
slides.notes: LIVE DEMO. From the funnel's dropped-off users, choose a stream with replay and play the prepared session. Skip inactivity. Name only what is visible; don't turn one replay into a population claim. The next chart checks whether the path is common. CUT: play 20 seconds from the bookmarked moment instead of starting at the session open.

slides.title: Journeys
points: Start from the event before the funnel drop
Compare Pathfinder and Journey Map
Expand or exclude an event to test the explanation
slides.notes: LIVE DEMO. Open the prepared Journeys chart. Show the common next actions after the step before drop-off. Expand one event by property or exclude a noisy event. Mention that Journeys uses the earliest path and may hide inactive events, so its totals needn't match the funnel exactly. CUT: if behind, show the saved result without editing it.

slides.title: From behavior to Braze
points: Behavioral cohort
Identity mapping
Braze segment
slides.caption: A cohort becomes useful in Braze only when the same person can be matched in both systems.
slides.notes: LIVE DEMO. Save the prepared behavioral condition as a cohort, open Sync, choose the configured Braze target, and show cadence. Then show where the cohort appears as an Amplitude Cohorts filter in Braze. Call out the identity requirement: Braze matches existing users; it doesn't create them. CUT: use an already-synced cohort and show the destination plus Braze segment.

slides.title: Guide with Experiment
points: Target a cohort
Control sees no guide
Variant sees the guide
slides.caption: The exposure fires when the user actually receives the assigned experience.
slides.notes: LIVE DEMO. Open the prepared guide, show targeting, then Add experiment. Explain the control and variant experience and open Manage Experiment to show the goal and allocation. Use Preview mode for appearance and a test user for runtime behavior. CUT: show the saved experiment configuration and prepared results. GATE: at 0:38 move to the data model whatever is unfinished. The hands-on hour does not absorb demo overrun.

slides.title: What arrives in Amplitude
points: A user does something
The app sends an event
Amplitude joins context and identity
slides.caption: Charts can only use distinctions that the instrumentation preserves.
slides.notes: Move from consuming data to producing it. Every chart in the speed run depended on event order, event context, and identity. The exercise starts from user behavior and works forward into that model.

slides.title: Three parts of the tracking plan
slides.notes: Use one concrete example. Event names describe completed actions. Event properties belong to one occurrence. User properties describe the person and remain available on later events until changed.

slides.title: Identity changes the analysis
slides.notes: Drive the panel live. Add two anonymous events, then sign in and add a third: the device's earlier activity resolves to the person, which is why the Braze cohort in the first hour had somebody to match. Then untick Set a user ID and add more events to show sign-in becoming invisible to analytics. IDs need at least five characters under the SDK default. Don't use an email address for this exercise.

slides.title: Five-minute reset
points: Open the workshop hub
Keep Amplitude open in another tab
Pair up if account access is blocked
slides.notes: Start the five-minute timer. Put the hub URL on screen. Use the break to pair anyone who can't create a project with someone who can.

slides.title: Design it, connect it, inspect it
points: Tracking plan
To-do app
New Amplitude project
slides.notes: Protect the remaining hour. Ask everyone to open the participant guide and app from the hub. The last station is optional.

slides.title: The app already works
points: Add, edit, complete, filter, delete, and share tasks
Edit event names in the Instrumentation panel
Watch every attempted event in the Activity panel
slides.notes: DEMO THE APP. Add a task, complete it, and open the Instrumentation panel. Show that task text appears in the interface but isn't sent as an event property. Change one event name and untick one event, and point out that both land in the URL. Don't connect an API key yet.

slides.title: Choose events
points: Read the eight user actions in the guide
Choose the actions worth tracking and name each event
Write one question each chosen event should answer
slides.notes: Give pairs 12 minutes. Ask them to name completed actions, not interface controls. Untick anything they decide not to track; that choice changes what the app sends. When checking progress, ask what decision each event supports. At minute 75, tell the room they have four minutes left.

slides.title: The user actions
points: Create, complete, reopen, edit
Delete and filter
Share and open a shared list
slides.notes: Leave this slide up while pairs work. All eight actions are also in the guide. They don't have to instrument every action; choosing not to track something is part of the plan.

slides.title: Add properties
points: Add context needed to answer each event question
Define role, analytics experience, and workshop table as user properties
Give every property a type and example value
slides.notes: Give pairs 12 minutes. Push for types and example values. Ask whether a proposed user property describes the person or only the latest action. Remind them that free-text task content can contain private data and isn't needed for the planned questions.

slides.title: Check each property

points.label: Use
points.title: A chart needs it
points.body: The property changes a filter, group, or interpretation.

points.label: Type
points.title: Its type is stable
points.body: Number stays number; boolean stays boolean.

points.label: Privacy
points.title: It avoids task text
points.body: Length can answer the question without collecting content.

slides.notes: Use these checks when the room asks what belongs in the plan. More properties don't automatically make better data.

slides.title: Connect Amplitude
points: Create a blank Amplitude project
Copy its API key into the app connection panel
Set your profile and send user properties
slides.notes: Demo the project settings path in the room's Amplitude account, then let attendees work. The app uses the Browser SDK and disables automatic tracking so every workshop event is intentional. Pair anyone blocked by permissions.

slides.title: Connection details
points: Use a project API key, never a secret key
Use the generated analyst ID instead of an email address
Choose US or EU to match the Amplitude project
slides.notes: Keep this visible during connection. The API key is a public client-side identifier. The app stores exercise state in the URL, so participants should still avoid putting personal or secret values into the fields.

slides.title: Generate and verify events
points: Perform at least three different actions in the app
Compare the Activity payload with your tracking plan
Find your user stream in Amplitude and inspect properties
slides.notes: Allow 12 minutes. Events may take a short time to appear. Have attendees search for their generated user ID. If an event is missing, check the app response, ad blockers, project region, and API key before changing the schema.

slides.title: When an event is missing
points: App Activity response
Browser network request
Amplitude user stream
slides.caption: Find the first place the expected event disappears.
slides.notes: Use the sequence as a fast debugging guide. The app records both preview payloads and SDK responses. Ad blockers can block the SDK or requests. A US/EU mismatch sends data to the wrong endpoint for the project.

slides.title: Ask one question
points: Choose one question from your plan
Build a small Event Segmentation or Funnel chart
Write down what your tiny workshop sample cannot tell you
slides.notes: This station is the buffer. If there are fewer than six minutes left, skip the build and ask two people which chart they would make. The sample is too small for a real product conclusion; the point is testing whether the schema supports the query.

slides.title: Keep the question with the event
slides.subtitle: The app, guide, and reference plan stay available from the workshop hub.
slides.notes: Close on the working habit: record the question beside the event and property definitions. Thank the room and leave the hub URL visible.
